gloss: to make light of; to belittle; to underestimate

definitions.gloss: to make light of; to belittle; to underestimate
definitions.explanation: To treat something as unimportant or less significant than it actually is. To give inadequate attention or respect to something that deserves more.

examples.japanese: {安全|あんぜん}を{軽視|けいし}してはならない。
examples.english: You must not make light of safety.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{意見|いけん}を{軽視|けいし}するべきではない。
examples.english: You should not dismiss his opinion.

examples.japanese: {基礎|きそ}{研究|けんきゅう}が{軽視|けいし}されると、{長期的|ちょうきてき}な{技術|ぎじゅつ}{発展|はってん}に{影響|えいきょう}が{出|で}る。
examples.english: When basic research is undervalued, it affects long-term technological development.

notes:
The opposite of {重視|じゅうし}する (to value highly, to take seriously). Carries a critical tone, implying that the thing being {軽視|けいし}された deserves more attention.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {安全|あんぜん}を{軽視|けいし}する: to neglect safety
- {人権|じんけん}を{軽視|けいし}する: to disregard human rights
- {軽視|けいし}できない: cannot be taken lightly
- {軽視|けいし}されがちな: tends to be overlooked

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {重視|じゅうし}する: to value, to regard as important — the antonym, meaning to give proper weight and attention to something
- {無視|むし}する: to ignore — stronger than {軽視|けいし}; means to completely disregard, while {軽視|けいし} means to give insufficient attention
- {見下|みくだ}す: to look down on — specifically directed at people and implies contempt, while {軽視|けいし} can apply to concepts, issues, and opinions as well
